Subject: Model output cut off mid-token in live checkout flow

We saw a couple of production sessions this morning where the model appears to stop mid-token during the checkout confirmation step. Example: the assistant outputed '...and we'll process the transac' and then the stream ended. No stop tokens were set on our side.

High level: this is intermittent (roughly 3 occurrences in last 2 hours), affects the cart confirmation completion, and is customer-visible. Attaching a screenshot and the example prompt file.

Session IDs / request IDs we captured: req_4f9b2a, req_4f9b8c, req_4f9d01. Timestamps (PST): 2026-11-22T08:57:31Z, 2026-11-22T09:01:04Z.

Can you confirm whether anything on Redwood's side could cause early stream termination (e.g., token clipping, batching boundary bug, or request timeouts)?

Thanks,
Tina Lopez

FreshMart

Hi all,

We completed an initial triage against the request details Tina provided. Summary of findings:

- Reproduction: we replayed the provided raw payloads against the same model variant and configuration (redwood/llama-3o-70b-v2, streaming enabled) for 200 attempts across our hosted cluster. We did not observe early termination or partial-token cutoffs in any of the replays.

- Platform logs: request traces for req_4f9b2a, req_4f9b8c, req_4f9d01 show normal lifecycle: request accepted, tokens produced, stream flush events recorded, final response sent. No internal timeout, OOM, or serving exception was logged. Attached: redwood_request_logs_20261122.csv (server-side trace snippets).

- Streaming/Chunking: our streaming implementation flushes at chunk boundaries; it will not intentionally cut a multibyte token mid-byte. We instrumented low-level stream frames for the replays and saw chunk boundaries align with UTF-8 token boundaries.

Possible causes to check on FreshMart side:
- Intermediate proxy or gateway terminating the HTTP/2 stream early (we have seen connection resets cause apparent truncated outputs).
- Client socket read code treating a transient connection close as a completed response (client-side parser bug).

Next steps we recommend:
1) If you can, capture one occurrence with a full packet capture or a server <-> client side trace (we can help interpret).
2) For the next test runs, set a unique request header (X-Debug-Run: freshmart-<id>) so we can correlate easily.
3) If it reproduces again, share a full request/response raw capture and we will escalate to infra to run a deeper network trace.

Given our replays and the absence of server-side errors, we don't see evidence of a Redwood serving bug at this time. If you want, we can schedule a joint debugging session to run a live repro with packet capture.

Attaching logs and the list of internal trace IDs we used for replay.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Model output cut off mid-token in live checkout flow — investigation summary and closure

Hi Tina,

Thanks for working with us on this. To summarize the investigation:
- We replayed the provided requests against the same model/version and could not reproduce the token-drop behavior.
- Server-side traces for your request IDs show normal completion and no internal errors, OOMs, or deliberate token truncation.
- Streaming code confirms chunk boundaries align to token boundaries and should not produce mid-token truncation.

Because we could not find platform-side evidence, we think the most likely cause is a client/proxy/networking issue at FreshMart (intermittent connection reset or a client-side stream parser treating a partial frame as final). Dylan outlined recommended next steps if it recurs.

As a courtesy for the inconvenience and to make future debugging easier, we've added 1,000 free inference units to your account and will run a live joint debugging session if you can reproduce. If you want to schedule a session, please send a couple of windows that work for you.

If you don't see further occurrences after trying the diagnostics, we'll close this ticket in HubSpot (FM-4982) in three business days.

Appreciate the signal — let us know if you want us to join a live run.

Best,
Jordan Blake
